lesson.title: Child sexual abuse material
lesson.summary: Use the incorporated child-abuse material/performance definitions and check national-law qualifications without graphic content.

prerequisites.reason: The incorporated material/performance definitions require following exact legal locators.
The learner must distinguish the action and purpose elements from the material definition.

blocks: The new point (bb) addresses AI generating or manipulating material or performance within Directive 2011/93/EU Article 2(c) and (e). The **incorporated-definition lookup** is essential: a cross-reference supplies part of the legal test.

The Directive defines a child as under 18. Its material definitions include specified real/simulated depictions, persons appearing to be children, and realistic synthetic depictions. We teach the lookup without images or graphic examples.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(bb), 5(1a); Article 113(a)

blocks: Article 2(e) concerns a live exhibition aimed at an audience, including via communication technology, with specified child sexual-abuse content. A file and a live performance need comparison with the appropriate incorporated definitions.
A synthetic origin does not by itself exclude the realistic-material category. Do not invent a blanket 'no real child means lawful' rule.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(bb), 5(1a); Article 113(a)

blocks: The **generation/manipulation ban** includes an exception where a 'without right' defence applies under national law. This requires the actual national provision and facts; it is not a self-declared exemption.

Our fictional safeguarding case leaves jurisdiction unspecified. The correct outcome is to identify the national-law question, not assume a defence or give a jurisdiction-specific permission without a source.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(bb), 5(1a); Article 113(a)

blocks: Point (bb) and paragraph 1a apply from **2 December 2026** in the working baseline. The next lesson separates supplier and deployer tests. Other criminal and safeguarding law remains independently relevant.

An assessment needs the incorporated content category, actor/action, date and any verified national-law qualification. No creation, demonstration or storage of abusive material is needed to learn this legal method.
